data.title: AST SpaceMobile Stock (ASTS) Rises in Premarket Even After Berenberg Downgrade — Here's Why
data.description:
AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) stock trended higher in Friday's pre-market trading even after Berenberg analyst Michael Filatov downgraded the stock to Hold from Buy and slashed his price target by 67.4% to $30 from $92. Filatov cited slower satellite launches as the reason for the downgrade, saying they delay the revenue growth needed to fund further satellite deployment.

Friday's gains come as U.S. futures rise ahead of the shortened session. Asian tech and chip stocks also rebounded after a steep sell-off, giving other growth stocks a lift.

Why Berenberg Downgraded AST SpaceMobile

Berenberg downgraded AST SpaceMobile because satellite launches have fallen behind its earlier expectations. When Filatov initiated coverage with a Buy rating in September, he expected the company to build toward 248 satellites. He also assumed launches from multiple providers would keep pace with satellite production. Instead, delays have slowed the rollout and the revenue growth needed to fund more satellites.

Filatov said Berenberg's view of AST SpaceMobile's technology and long-term economics remains unchanged. His concern is the company's reliance on launch capacity it does not control. He believes Blue Origin accounts for much of that capacity, making its launch schedule important to AST SpaceMobile's expansion plans.

As Filatov explained, "the path to scale depends on launch capacity ASTS does not control."

Berenberg Now Expects a 100-Satellite Network by 2028

Given the slower launch pace, Berenberg now expects AST SpaceMobile to complete its funded constellation of about 100 satellites in 2028. The firm expects the company to hold its network at that size until free cash flow turns positive in 2030. This is a slower rollout than the earlier plan to reach 248 satellites.

Blue Origin's next New Glenn launch could also influence Berenberg's outlook. Filatov said a successful return to flight would lead the firm to reconsider its rating. "Another failure or a long slip would create downside risk," he warned.

Is ASTS Stock a Buy Now? 

In contrast to Berenberg, B. Riley analyst Mike Crawford has turned more positive on AST SpaceMobile after its recent share price decline. Last week, the 5-star analyst upgraded the stock to Buy from Neutral while maintaining his $48 price target.

Crawford believes the recent share price decline has priced in much of the funding and launch risk, creating a better risk-reward opportunity. He also sees potential in AST SpaceMobile's rocket development plans, saying "much of that risk is priced in."

Wall Street remains constructive on the stock. AST SpaceMobile carries a Moderate Buy consensus rating based on six Buys and four Holds over the past three months. The average ASTS price target stands at $63.39, suggesting 143.60% upside from current levels. Year-to-date, ASTS stock has declined 64%.

data.title: Google and Los Angeles Schools Clash over AI Features and Search Access
data.description:
Los Angeles Unified School District (LAUSD) has reportedly disabled Google's (GOOGL) AI-generated search summaries, known as AI Overviews, on school-issued devices. With around 500,000 students, LAUSD is now the largest school district to block the feature. The move comes amid concerns over Google's refusal to offer a way to separate its search service from AI tools used in education.

The LAUSD did not formally announce its decision to disable Google's AI Overviews, leaving many parents and students surprised. Bridie Lee, a leader of Schools Beyond Screens LA, said the move "was the talk of the playground." The group supports screen-time limits and better oversight of technology in schools.

Google Faces Wider School Backlash

Google is widely used in U.S. schools, with its Chromebooks and apps like Google Docs and Classroom used by students and teachers. The company's push to add AI features has drawn criticism from schools worried about how the technology could affect learning.

In September, New York City banned generative AI for students through eighth grade for the 2026–27 school year, affecting nearly 600,000 children.

In response, Google announced earlier this month that it will turn off Google Search and its AI tools by default for K-12 student accounts unless schools choose to enable them. However, schools that want students to use Google Search must also accept its built-in AI features, as Google does not offer a separate option to turn them off.

Google's AI Ambitions Come at a Cost

Google's AI push also comes with risks. The company has acknowledged that AI Mode earns less per query than traditional search links, raising concerns about how AI could affect its main source of income.

In Q3 2026, GOOGL stock lost as much as $500 billion in market value as investors grew concerned about AI costs and pressure on its search business. Search revenue grew 12% year-over-year, down from 17% in Q2 and 19% in Q1.

Alphabet also spent $51.4 billion on capital expenses, while operating cash flow was $42.3 billion. This left the company with negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion as it continued to invest in data centers and power infrastructure.

Is Google Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Overall, Wall Street analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on GOOGL stock based on 30 Buys and four Holds assigned in the past three months. The average GOOGL price target of $399.58 per share implies a 46.3% upside potential.

GOOGL currently trades at $270.98, down 13.6% year-to-date.

data.title: Anthropic and Meta Eye Data Center Projects with Japan's JERA
data.description:
JERA, Japan's largest power company, is reportedly in talks with Anthropic (ANT), Meta (META), and other U.S. tech firms to build data centers near power plants in the Tokyo area. Nikkei reported, citing an interview with JERA Global CEO and Chairman Yukio Kani, that the company is also holding talks with Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT), and Google (GOOGL).

For context, JERA is a 50-50 joint venture between Tokyo Electric Power Company (TKECF) and Chubu Electric Power Company (CHUEFF). The company is involved in power generation, fuel procurement, and energy trading. It also has a major role in Japan's electricity supply.

JERA's $15 Billion AI Data Center Plan

JERA plans to use electricity from its own power plants to supply these data centers. This could help cut the long wait times for grid connections.

The first project is planned at the Chiba Thermal Power Station, with a capacity of up to 400 megawatts (MW) and an investment of more than $15 billion. The facility is expected to begin operations around 2028.

In October, JERA signed agreements with Dell Technologies (DELL) and RHAELM to develop AI infrastructure in Japan. The plan is to combine power supply, cooling systems, and computing equipment into a single model that can be used at other thermal power plants.

Power Supply Emerges as a Key Bottleneck in the AI Race

Power is becoming a major challenge for the AI industry. Companies need more electricity to run their AI data centers, and getting enough power from the grid can take time. AI companies are seeking more direct control over the infrastructure needed to run their models. Anthropic currently relies heavily on cloud providers for computing resources.

Tech giants are now looking at ways to get electricity directly from power plants. If JERA's plan works, it could help data centers start operations faster. It could also give Japan's unused thermal power plants a new role and allow power companies to move beyond selling electricity to helping build AI infrastructure.

Is Anthropic Stock a Good Buy?

On TipRanks, ANT stock has a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 10 Buys and one Hold rating. The average Anthropic price target of $150.5 implies 82% upside potential from current levels.

data.title: U.S. Stock Futures in Focus Ahead of a Shortened Black Friday Session
data.description:
U.S. stock futures rose sharply ahead of Friday's shortened trading session, with Nasdaq-100 futures leading the gains. U.S. equity markets were closed on Nov. 26 for Thanksgiving and will reopen from 9:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. ET on Friday. Trading volumes are expected to be light as many investors take time off for the holiday weekend.

Futures on the Nasdaq-100 (NDX), the S&P 500 Index (SPX), and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) were up 2.89%, 1.74%, and 0.87%, respectively, as of 1:41 a.m. EST on November 27.

Meanwhile, oil prices climbed in Asian trading, remaining near monthly highs. Attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy sites have raised concerns about supply. Both Brent and WTI crude are on track for their first weekly gains in four weeks.

At the time of writing, Brent crude futures, the international benchmark, rose 0.80% to $97.32 per barrel, while WTI crude futures were up 3.11% at $86.28 per barrel.

The major indexes remain on track for strong weekly gains, based on Wednesday's close, even as AI stocks have given back some of their early gains. The S&P 500 is up nearly 4% for the week, while the Nasdaq Composite and Dow have gained more than 4%.

The rally began Monday after Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia (NVDA) CEO, sending the stock up 31.5%. The rebound helped the S&P 500 and Nasdaq post their best sessions since April 2025, while the Dow gained more than 1,400 points, or roughly 3%.

data.title: 'Finding New Frontiers': Mizuho Recommends 2 Lesser-Known Space Stocks to Buy
data.description:
Space may be the final frontier, but right now, it is also the expanding frontier of exploration and business – and the two are not as mutually exclusive as the idealists would have us believe. For better or worse, the profit motive is driving the space economy, and an array of companies is moving to establish niches and gain market share. Giants like SpaceX or upstarts like Rocket Lab may be in the lead right now, but they are not the only players on the 'space board.'

The numbers offer some perspective on the scale of the opportunity. According to a September report from the OECD, global space-related revenues reached an estimated $550 billion to $600 billion in 2025, approaching the size of the semiconductor industry. Meanwhile, private operators accounted for 88% of satellites launched last year, compared with just 23% in 2010, illustrating how much of the activity has shifted toward commercial enterprises.

Smaller companies can frequently offer investors greater upside potential, particularly in an industry undergoing such rapid expansion. They usually focus on more specialized segments, offering unique services or proprietary technology to meet specific customer needs in terms of capability or pricing.

Among those looking beyond the industry's more familiar names is Mizuho analyst Greg Konrad, who believes investors need to be selective when deciding where to put their money.

"We are bullish on the growth in space, but a bit more selective on the stocks. Space revenue is growing far faster than anything else we cover. Launch is cheap enough that demand is real, the Moon and the defense space domain are adding buyers, and the highest opportunity companies are vertically integrated. The risk is execution and sometimes risk-off as the group itself tends to trade together. Nonetheless we do have to pick winners and sometimes that is the business itself and sometimes it is correlating the business to its valuation. That is somewhat why the divergence in the group," Konrad opined.

So let's follow this line of thought and look at two lesser-known space stocks that Konrad believes are worth buying at current levels. Based on the TipRanks database, we'll also find out whether the rest of Wall Street shares his enthusiasm.

MDA Space, Ltd. (MDA)

We'll start in the great frozen north, where MDA Space is Canada's largest developer and manufacturer of space technology. The company is based in Ontario and has been in operation since 1969. Historically, MDA worked in industrial control systems, portable ground stations for satellite monitoring, and high-end radar systems; today, it is known for its work in robotics, satellites, and geointelligence.

MDA has long experience in developing and supporting space infrastructure, from providing supportive technology to NASA's space shuttle program to independently putting together commercial space robotic technology. The company has also expanded its defense offerings with MDA MIDNIGHT, a spacecraft designed to protect critical assets in orbit.

One of MDA's most important areas of operation is in satellite communications. The company's Aurora program is a product line of software-defined digital satellites, offering users the capability to dynamically adjust coverage and bandwidth for increased system flexibility and functionality. MDA supports Aurora by designing and prototyping the necessary ASIC semiconductors in-house, although the large-scale fabrication is sent to third-party foundries.

Space technology is a global domain, and MDA employs more than 4,000 people worldwide, primarily in Canada, the US, the UK, and Israel. The company's own facility footprint is extensive – it has more than 1 million square feet of floor space for offices, labs, design facilities, and manufacturing lines.

MDA is also pursuing two acquisitions: US-based spacecraft manufacturer Blue Canyon Technologies (BCT) and a majority stake in French satellite data and analytics provider Collecte Localisation Satellites (CLS).

This all adds up to big business, and for 3Q26, MDA reported a work backlog of C$3.9 billion. This is an important metric, providing 'revenue visibility' into next year and further on.

In the meantime, MDA generated C$498.1 million in revenue for the third quarter this year, a figure that was up 21.5% year-over-year. The gross profit, at C$125.9 million, was up 16.6% from the year-ago period.

Against this backdrop, Mizuho's Konrad believes MDA stands out in an industry where commercial opportunities do not necessarily translate into attractive investment propositions.

"MDA is Canada's national space champion and one of the few highly profitable companies in space, now priming whole constellations on its AURORA software-defined satellites and in-house application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) chips. Blue Canyon Technologies (BCT) adds U.S. defense access, and CLS adds recurring data and analytics. Our thesis rests on three points: 1) total revenue +49% in 2027E, including +11% organic; 2) a C$3.95BB backlog, ~1.8x 2027E total organic revenue, with a C$40BB pipeline behind it; and 3) a 19.0% adjusted EBITDA margin in 2027E with both deals included. We value MDA Space at 18.0x 2028E EBITDA, a ~35% premium to the space/defense tech peer median of 13.3x, reflecting its high margins, growth and M&A catalysts," Konrad noted.

And just how much money could investors stand to make here? Konrad rates MDA shares an Outperform (i.e., Buy), with a $44 price target implying upside potential of 61.5% from current levels. (To watch Konrad's track record, click here)

Overall, MDA's Strong Buy consensus rating is unanimous, based on 11 recent positive analyst reviews. The stock's current trading price of $27.24 and average target price of $41.35 together indicate a one-year potential gain of ~52%. (See MDA stock forecast)

BlackSky Technology (BKSY)

Now we'll turn to BlackSky, another company in the field of commercial geospatial intelligence satellites. The company is based in Herndon, Virginia – putting it in close proximity to the US government agencies and Pentagon contractors that are putting a high premium on quality space technology.

BlackSky currently operates a constellation of proprietary satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO), and uses AI-powered software analytics to deliver high-end real-time imagery and insights for a wide range of customers. The company primarily serves US and international government and defense customers, although it also caters to commercial clients.

The company's customers can tap into BlackSky's network of satellites and analytics, which promise 'space-based intelligence at the speed of conflict.' That's a vital feature, differentiating BlackSky as a high-end service provider – in today's fast-paced digital world, yesterday's information can already be outdated.

BlackSky sets itself apart from the competition by leaning directly into that. Its satellite constellations are 'high-revisit' – that is, they consistently make repeat flights over strategic locations, economic assets, and events around the world. Their communications are low-latency, allowing for a fast pace of high- and very-high-resolution imagery, delivered by a first-of-its-kind platform optimized for today's needs. Customers can receive data, composed of real-time imagery and automated, AI-driven analytics, with an average delivery time of 90 minutes or less.

We should note an important recent move that expands BlackSky's ability to deliver comprehensive solutions for real-time intelligence on the world's most important locations with the detail needed to support fast decision-making. Earlier this month, BlackSky announced its acquisition of EpochGeo. EpochGeo is a geospatial data science firm that specializes in artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) solutions from multiple data sources, including RF and signals intelligence, and applies those capabilities in the defense sector. The financial details of the acquisition were not disclosed.

In its 3Q26 report, BlackSky's revenue hit a company quarterly record of $43 million. This was up 118% year-over-year and beat the forecast by $2.87 million. The company also reached another milestone, reporting its first quarterly operating profit of $405,000. The GAAP diluted EPS came to 10 cents, a sharp turnaround from the 44-cent loss reported for 3Q25, and it beat expectations by 34 cents per share.

While BlackSky's latest results offer encouragement, Konrad sees reasons to be bullish that extend well beyond the company's recent financial performance.

"The market under-appreciates how BKSY's model has evolved from a U.S.-reliant supplier of satellite-based imagery to a global provider of vertically integrated imagery satellite systems and services. This has been driven by the evolution of its enhanced Gen-3 satellite constellation, AROS development, along with its emergence as a seller of the satellite systems themselves. Thesis tied to: 1) Sustainable ~30% revenue growth on an enhanced satellite constellation and a growing satellite prime business; 2) adjusted EBITDA-positive today (15.2% EBITDA margin in 2026E) with a runway to 40.7% margins by 2029E; and 3) a balance sheet that can fund near-term investments," the analyst wrote.

Konrad backs up his bullish stance with an Outperform (i.e., Buy) rating and a $37 price target that implies about 132% upside from current levels.

All in all, BlackSky's stock has earned a Strong Buy consensus rating on the Street based on 4 recent analyst reviews, including 3 Buys and 1 Hold. The stock is selling for $15.97 and its $37.13 average target price is practically the same as Konrad's. (See BKSY stock forecast)

data.title: Musk Pledges One More SpaceX Share Annually for Each U.S. Child – What It Means for Current Holders
data.description:
Elon Musk has pledged to give one more SpaceX (SPCX) share to each U.S. child annually. The move adds to a plan that would give each child with an active Trump Account one share from SpaceX and one from Musk.

The new pledge raises questions about how the gifts will affect the share count and Musk's stake. Musk has yet to say when the yearly gifts will start or how long they will last.

SpaceX's Share Count and Musk's Stake

SpaceX had about 13.58 billion shares out as of October 15, 2026, based on its 10-Q filing. This included about 8.25 billion Class A shares and 5.33 billion Class B shares. The Class A shares trade on Nasdaq under the ticker SPCX, while Class B shares are not listed.

Musk held about 6.42 billion shares, or about 48% of the firm, as of June 30, 2026. His stake includes shares held by trusts, restricted shares, and stock options. He also held more than 82% of the voting power, per a company filing.

Will the Gift Dilute Current Holders?

SpaceX plans to issue one new Class A share to each active Trump Account, starting in December. Musk plans to give a share from his own stake once his lockup ends in June 2027. His gift would not add to the share count, but it would reduce his stake.

If SpaceX issues 70 million new shares, the share count would rise by about 0.53%. That would trim the ownership share of current holders by about the same rate. It would not mean the stock price must fall by 0.53%.

The White House said in October that nearly 70 million accounts had been opened, with more than 60 million set up by auto-enrollment. At the Nov. 25 close of $127.44 a share, two shares for each of 70 million accounts would be worth about $17.8 billion.

Trump Accounts are tax-advantaged stock accounts for U.S. kids under 18. They allow up to $5,000 in after-tax funds each year. The U.S. Treasury also gives a one-time $1,000 seed sum to kids born from 2025 through 2028.

The pledge also adds to other gifts tied to Trump Accounts. SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell and her husband pledged a share of their holdings to more than 2 million kids in October.

Is SPCX Stock a Good Buy or Sell?

On TipRanks, SPCX has a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 28 Buys, six Holds, and one Sell. The average SpaceX price target of $265 implies 107.9% upside potential from the November 25 closing price of $127.44.

data.title: MongoDB Q3 Earnings Preview – Here's What Wall Street Expects from MDB Stock
data.description:
Database software company MongoDB (MDB) will announce its fiscal third-quarter results on December 1. Wall Street expects MDB's Q3 FY27 earnings per share (EPS) to grow 22% year-over-year to $1.61. Revenue is projected to grow 21.4% to $762.5 million, reflecting solid demand for its products.

The sudden departure of CEO Chirantan Desai to join Meta Platforms (META) as Chief Enterprise Platform Officer and concerns that AI models could impact traditional software businesses have weighed on MDB stock this year. However, most analysts are bullish on MongoDB stock and see solid upside potential.

Analysts' Views Ahead of MongoDB's Q3 Earnings

Heading into Q3 FY27 earnings, RBC Capital analyst Rishi Jaluria reiterated a Buy rating on MongoDB stock with a price target of $465. The analyst noted the 25% year-to-date decline in MDB stock and agreed that investors are cautious about the CEO transition. Given the pullback, he finds the stock's risk/reward attractive at about 7x 2027 revenue. Jaluria noted that checks at MDB.local NYC and the company's disclosures on AI-native workloads were constructive.

The analyst highlighted that the AI-native customer count has almost doubled over the trailing two years. Also, Atlas revenue from AI natives grew 165% year-over-year in Q2 FY27. Jaluria continues to view MongoDB as the "database vendor of choice for net new GenAI applications," with the share of Atlas ARR (annual recurring revenue) from customers with at least one AI use case rising 30% year-over-year in Q2 FY27 to about 40% of the total.  

Meanwhile, Citi analyst Tyler Radke reiterated a Buy rating on MDB stock but cut his price target to $525 from $565 to reflect a slightly lower multiple. The analyst remains "positive" on the company ahead of the fiscal third-quarter earnings and maintains his above-street estimates. Notably, Radke expects MongoDB to deliver about 29% growth in Atlas and raise the Q4 implied guidance.

Radke added that his fieldwork remained favorable, as large enterprise migrations at financial services and healthcare were strong. Also, a few AI labs increased their usage this quarter. Radke thinks that investor expectations are low ahead of Q3 FY27 earnings, with shares of MDB and other usage-based software peers under pressure since the last quarter. Nevertheless, MongoDB remains a "top pick" for Radke. He expects growth to keep accelerating as AI labs and AI-native customers ramp up their use cases. Radke also cited tailwinds from enterprise modernization and AI adoption among enterprise customers.

Is MDB a Good Stock to Buy?

Ahead of Q3 FY27 earnings, Wall Street has a Strong Buy consensus rating on MongoDB stock based on 28 Buys and three Holds. The average MDB stock price target of $459.96 indicates about 47% upside potential.

data.title: Rocket Lab Books over $515 Million in Launches for a Rocket That Hasn't Flown Yet
data.description:
Space launch company Rocket Lab (RKLB) has secured more than $515 million in orders for its Neutron rocket, even though the rocket has never flown. The company signed eight missions with five customers during the third quarter, despite Neutron's first flight being delayed until 2027. Several customers agreed to a base launch price of $70 million, up by $15 million from the earlier $55 million rate. This means that customers are reserving flights years before Rocket Lab has proved that Neutron can reach orbit.

Neutron is designed to carry up to 13,000 kilograms into low Earth orbit. That would allow Rocket Lab to serve customers with larger satellites than its smaller Electron rocket can carry.

Next Available Launch Slots Are Now in the 2030s

For example, Finnish satellite operator ICEYE booked three launches starting in late 2028. U.S. satellite company Muon Space reserved two more for 2029 and 2030. Starcloud also booked a 2029 mission for its proposed space-based computer facilities. Meanwhile, Canada's Kepler Communications and the U.S. Space Force each reserved one launch. These orders brought Neutron's total bookings to 16 missions. Rocket Lab says its next available launch slots are now in the 2030s.

The higher prices suggest that customers are willing to pay more for additional rocket capacity. If Neutron starts seeing regular use, those contracts could become a meaningful source of revenue. However, the $515 million represents future launch commitments, not money already earned.

Still, Rocket Lab's existing business provides some support while Neutron is developed. Its order backlog reached $3.57 billion in September, up by 52% from June. In addition, quarterly revenue grew by 73% from a year earlier to $268 million. Its smaller Electron rocket also completed its 100th launch on November 14.

Risks to Watch Out For

The biggest obstacle is getting Neutron off the ground. In October, engineers found defects in a part of its first-stage fuel tank. The company had to produce a replacement, which pushed the debut from 2026 into 2027, as the replacement part still needs further testing.

Rocket Lab must also assemble the full first stage and test how it handles pressure and extremely cold fuel before the inaugural flight. As a result, more delays could push back when the company earns revenue from its contracts and increase development costs. For context, Rocket Lab reported a third-quarter loss of $0.12 per share despite record revenue.

Management has not announced a specific 2027 launch date and plans to provide a more precise schedule after the remaining fuel tank tests.

Is RKLB Stock a Good Buy?

Turning to Wall Street, TipRanks data shows that analysts have a Moderate Buy consensus rating on RKLB stock. This is based on 15 Buys, three Holds, and one Sell assigned in the past three months. Furthermore, the average RKLB price target of $92.33 per share implies 96.4% upside potential. (See RKLB Stock Forecast).

data.title: IREN Stock Is Down 66% YTD — Why Analysts Still See 340% Upside Ahead
data.description:
Shares in AI data center operator IREN Limited (IREN) have plunged by roughly 66% since the start of the year. IREN stock closed Wednesday's regular trading session at $12.85, near its 52-week low of $11.34. Still, Wall Street analysts see the stock rising about 340% over the next 12 months. This comes as several analysts have recently issued Buy ratings on the Sydney-based neocloud company.

Why IREN Shares Have Tumbled So Far in 2026

IREN shares have sold off this year for several reasons. These include the company's funding gap, Nvidia's (NVDA) leadership crisis, and results of the recent U.S. midterm elections.

  • Funding gap: During its fiscal Q1 2027 earnings call in early November, IREN revealed a key funding gap. It plans to spend $15 billion in fiscal 2027. It expects about $9 billion to come from cash and secured financing. That leaves a $6 billion funding gap.
  • Nvidia leadership crisis: Jensen Huang's recent brief resignation as Nvidia CEO led to a selloff in neocloud stocks. This appears to be driven by fears of reduced financial support for the industry from the AI chip giant.
  • U.S. midterm election: The election results also fueled fears of political pushback against rapid data center construction.
  • High borrowing costs: IREN shares also sold off amid reports that investors are demanding higher yields to fund AI projects. In October, billionaire executive Elon Musk warned that lenders are pulling back from AI cloud firms without significant revenue sources outside AI data centers. This added to the pressure.
  • Microsoft project delay: IREN shares also fell on news that Microsoft (MSFT) was tightening oversight of some data center projects. More importantly, IREN also recently shifted its annual recurring revenue (ARR) target timeline from year-end to January 2027. This shift was due to changes Microsoft requested on a data center project.


Why Analysts Are Backing IREN Limited

Bernstein analyst Madison Rezaei recently weighed in on IREN's ARR timeline shift. She argued that IREN's actual computing capacity remains contracted and funded. The analyst maintained her Buy rating on IREN shares.

Similarly, four-star Bernstein analyst Gautam Chhugani recently reaffirmed his Buy rating on IREN shares. Chhugani addressed concerns relating to Nvidia. He argued that IREN can build partnerships beyond Nvidia.

Is IREN a Good Stock to Buy Now?

On Wall Street, analysts have a Moderate Buy consensus rating on IREN's shares, according to TipRanks' data. This reflects eight Buys and three Holds assigned over the past three months.

However, the average IREN price target of $56.50 implies about 340% upside (see IREN stock forecast here).
